pages.title: MAG1 Full Manual — MAG1WW60-1 Development Firmware · V1.0
pages.description: This manual is for MAG1WW60-1 development software (MAG1CW60-1.pac, Android 15 / userdebug). The system displays the build as MAG1WW60-1. MAG1 also has WW53, MAG1WW60 and MAG1WW64 firmware versions; their features and procedures may differ. Existing WW53 captures and procedures are historical references and require re-verification on MAG1WW60-1. MAG1WW64 findings remain separately dated evidence.

System settings / about

Device information, versions and regulatory labels

Use this chapter to prepare and check the device information, versions and regulatory labels workflow on this firmware.

MAG1WW60-1 · dated captures available

This chapter uses MAG1WW60-1 evidence only. Reference steps are separate from the actions actually recorded.

Settings → About phone

Before you start

  • Keep serial numbers, IMEI and account identifiers out of public captures.

Reference steps · see recorded scope below

  1. Open About phone and locate the model, Android version and build information actually displayed.
  2. Record the firmware build alongside the guide revision when reporting a menu difference.
  3. Inspect regulatory or legal entries only if offered; do not infer certification from hardware-feature declarations.
  4. Check app versions separately in App info; system firmware alone does not identify Google component versions.

Options and scope

Reference procedure drafted; no new operation test or capture was performed.

MAG1WW60-1 observed scope

Android version details on the MAG1WW60-1 test device: Android 15 and patch/version fields. The original screen retains the internal software string MAG1WW60-1; no identifier page or update installation is shown.

Exit and restore

Return to the previous page. If you choose to try these steps, restore only settings changed for that test and remove only its test data.

Troubleshooting

  • If the menu differs, record firmware and app versions and use the controls actually shown. Stop when a required credential or accessory is unavailable.

System settings / accessibility

Accessibility, text, colors and assisted controls

Choose features for your visual, hearing or interaction needs and learn how to exit before enabling unfamiliar gestures.

MAG1WW60-1 · dated captures available

This chapter uses MAG1WW60-1 evidence only. Reference steps are separate from the actions actually recorded.

Settings → Accessibility

Before you start

  • Record the original settings
  • Read the exit instructions before enabling a screen reader, magnification or an accessibility menu
  • Use non-private content for testing

Reference steps · see recorded scope below

View dated screenshots and videos ↓

  1. Open Accessibility and browse the categories and features available on the device.
  2. Start with easily reversible font or display size changes and inspect the sample text. Sliders and reset buttons require subpage verification.
  3. Choose color and animation options for your needs and record their original values before changing them.
  4. A screen reader changes tapping and swiping behavior. Do not enable it as a default demonstration before verifying how to exit.
  5. Hearing and interaction aids may affect audio channels, touch input and shortcuts. Read and test each item separately.
  6. Change one setting at a time and record the result. Restore it before trying another if it does not suit your needs.

Security and recovery / accounts

Accounts, passwords, passkeys and sync

Use this chapter to prepare and check the accounts, passwords, passkeys and sync workflow on this firmware.

MAG1WW60-1 · dated captures available

This chapter uses MAG1WW60-1 evidence only. Reference steps are separate from the actions actually recorded.

Settings → Passwords, passkeys & accounts

Before you start

  • Keep account recovery available outside this phone.

Reference steps · see recorded scope below

  1. Review Preferred service to identify the selected password or autofill provider; avoid exposing saved credentials.
  2. Open the intended account and read the synchronization choices before changing them.
  3. Use Add account only for an account you control, completing sign-in and verification on the phone.
  4. Review Automatically sync personal data. Before removing an account, confirm needed contacts and files exist in another accessible location.

MAGNE, AI and Web3 / ai

On-device AI

Understand the models on MAG1, what they do, and which capabilities have been tested. Explore text, speech and imaging, then follow the desktop-control demonstration.

MAG1WW60-1 · dated captures available

This chapter uses MAG1WW60-1 evidence only. Reference steps are separate from the actions actually recorded.

Installed AI app → Its model and settings (each app requires verification)

Before you start

  • Test prompts without personal information
  • An authorized test account, model and network
  • Check the app prompts for model downloads, installation and any charges

Reference steps · see recorded scope below

  1. gptos.intelligence.assistant 2.1.570 was found as a user-installed package. Its presence does not establish that it is factory-installed MAGNE AI.
  2. Inventory each AI app in actual use separately, including sign-in, input, voice, images, model selection, history, files, permissions and account deletion.
  3. Test text input and results using a prompt without personal information. If an account is required, pause only that app's test.
  4. Verify offline capability per application, with model identity, network conditions, fresh output and network restoration recorded. Completed console and call-translation demonstrations are scoped below.
  5. Voice and image features involve microphone/camera permissions and uploads. Establish where processing occurs and the service conditions.
  6. Check generated results for accuracy and limitations. Model output is not official evidence of device specifications.

Buttons and options

Button / optionPurpose and limits
Model selectionA model name does not prove that it runs locally
HistoryMay contain personal information; not captured in the recorded demonstration
Voice / imagesPermissions and upload routes require separate verification
OfflineRequires evidence from testing without a network connection

MAG1WW60-1 observed scope

MAG1WW60-1 integrates dedicated camera visual-AI components and a separate local call-translation model path. The camera application and JN1 configuration contain scene-recognition, denoising, depth/segmentation and beauty components. Integration does not establish that every component executes in every mode.

In the MAG1WW60-1 call-translation test, the Qwen2.5-1.5B model service opened the NPU device and completed task counts increased after translation was enabled. This supports NPU use by that translation path. A subsequent DEMO produced new transcripts and translations with Wi-Fi and mobile data disabled; see the recorded test conditions below. The processor used by each ASR/TTS stage was not established.

Camera mode-by-mode runtime tracing remains pending. There is no current evidence that ordinary photography uses the translation language model, or that CPU, GPU and NPU simultaneously execute the same model.

MAGNE.AI x FIH · DESKTOP DEMO

On-device AI · Control MAG1 from your computer

This engineering console sends requests over local HTTP and USB / ADB to the connected MAG1, then displays the phone’s response. It is a development demonstration, not a preinstalled consumer app. Features continue to evolve.

MAG1WW60-1 · Android 15 · 2026-10-16 · UTC+08:00 · English interface

Computer→ USB / ADB →MAG1→Results on the computer

Watch a real request

Connection check → ASR transcription → independent TTS synthesis → playback. The overview contains saved results; the video then submits fresh requests.

Real browser frames are sampled in chronological order and held until the next frame; this is not a smooth, frame-complete screen recording. Use the returned metrics, not video duration, for timing. The playback soundtrack is this run’s generated WAV aligned with the Play action, not a room-microphone recording.

Open / download the video · Capture record and file hashes

Follow the workflow

  1. Connect the prepared MAG1 by USB, complete normal device authorization, start the local console, and choose English or Traditional Chinese.
  2. Select Check connection. Confirm MAG1WW60-1 and the required service state before testing.
  3. In Speech recognition, query languages and select Transcribe sample. Compare the returned text with “The weather is sunny today.” This tests a synthetic file, not live microphone capture.
  4. In Speech synthesis, choose the sample text, matching voice and speed; select Generate on phone. After success, play or download the WAV and review any warnings.
  5. Use Installed models to read each file’s purpose and evidence. File presence alone does not confirm active inference or acceleration.

Two separate execution paths

ModuleTested path and boundary
ASRMAGNE.AI x FIH service via Android Binder. The English sample returned a transcript. This does not establish every language or the accelerator used.
Kokoro TTSIndependent sherpa-onnx runtime on phone CPU, two threads. This demonstration does not invoke or repair the FIH TTS service, whose model-path mismatch remains.
GemmaSeparate model/runtime experiments are outside this recording; they are not presented as FIH SDK support.
What this recording establishes

The computer can control these prepared phone-side test paths and display real responses. Wi-Fi and mobile data remained enabled in this recording; it is not a new network-isolation test. The separately recorded offline call-translation demo below has its own conditions.

Screenshots you can inspect

Listen to this run’s output

Hello. This speech is generated locally on the MAG1 phone.

Audio 4.26 s · synthesis 9.45 s · RTF 2.22. Synthesis excludes model loading, USB transfer and playback. A single observation, not a benchmark average. Unknown-token / skipped-phoneme warnings were returned; pronunciation has not been independently scored.

This manual embeds static evidence. It does not connect visitors to the local control service. Running a test requires the prepared computer, console environment and an authorized MAG1 USB connection.

MAG1 · ON-DEVICE AI

On-device AI model guide

This covers every model-format file identified in the dated scan, additional compiled vendor candidates, and the separately installed Gemma experiment. It is not a claim that all models on the phone have been found: private app data, other APK archives and unrecognized proprietary formats remain outside the scan.

Language & speechSystem & visionCompiled vendor filesIndependent Gemma

A conceptual voice workflow is VAD → ASR → LLM → TTS: detect speech, transcribe it, generate or translate text, then speak it. This explains how the roles fit together; it does not claim that every MAG1 app uses all these exact files.

01 / Language and speech

Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct · UNIText generation and LLM translation
Input → output
Text prompt → generated text. Translation uses the same language model.
What it is for
Short answers, supplied-text summaries, drafting and translation. Generated facts still need checking.
How to use it
Console: Text generation or Text translation, using EDGE_ONLY. These controls call the firmware service; they do not offer arbitrary model-file replacement.
Recorded status and limits
Real text and translation service responses were recorded. The service code selects this UNI model path. Accelerator observations from the separate call-translation test do not prove the backend of every console request.
/product/media/models/llm/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-UNI/Qwen2.5-1.5B-a16w8-feo.unillm1,950.85 MiB
Paraformer · INT8Automatic speech recognition (ASR)
Input → output
Speech audio → a written transcript. It does not generate speech or translate by itself.
What it is for
Turn spoken words into text for dictation, captions or a later translation step. These are possible uses, not all verified product integrations.
How to use it
Console: Speech recognition → Query languages → Transcribe sample. The console currently tests the service, not a user-selectable Paraformer backend.
Recorded status and limits
The installed file is referenced in ASR code. The English sample returned text, but runtime tracing has not identified which ASR model handled it. The exposed service reports zh-CN and en-US.
/product/media/models/asr/sherpa-onnx-paraformer-zh-small-2024-03-09/model.int8.onnx78.04 MiB
SenseVoice · INT8Alternative speech-recognition model
Input → output
Speech audio → text through an alternative ASR configuration.
What it is for
An alternative recognition path when the application and runtime select the matching configuration.
How to use it
No independent model selector or dedicated SenseVoice test is exposed in the current console. Testing it separately requires a verified configuration or dedicated test program.
Recorded status and limits
The file and code reference are present; independent inference is untested. The zh-en-ja-ko-yue folder name does not establish Japanese, Korean or Cantonese support in the exposed service, nor other SenseVoice capabilities.
/product/media/models/asr/sherpa-onnx-sense-voice-zh-en-ja-ko-yue-2024-07-17/model.int8.onnx228.15 MiB
Silero VADVoice activity detection
Input → output
Audio segments → whether speech is present, helping identify speech start and end.
What it is for
Avoid sending long silences to ASR and divide speech into usable segments. VAD does not transcribe words or identify the speaker.
How to use it
A supporting stage inside the recognition pipeline, not a separate consumer app or current console button.
Recorded status and limits
ASR voice-activity code references this file. Endpoint accuracy and an independent VAD run have not been tested.
/product/media/models/asr/silero-vad/silero_vad.onnx2.22 MiB
Kokoro · multilingual v1.1Text-to-speech synthesis (TTS)
Input → output
Text + voice + speed → a speech waveform, saved here as WAV.
What it is for
Read answers, passages or translated text aloud. This complements ASR: one listens, the other speaks.
How to use it
Console: Speech synthesis → choose a matching voice → Generate on phone → Play / Download WAV. The demonstrated path is independent sherpa-onnx on phone CPU, two threads.
Recorded status and limits
English and Chinese WAV outputs were recorded. Original FIH TTS still expects model.int8.onnx, while model.onnx is installed. Independent success does not repair that mismatch. Runtime token/phoneme warnings remain; pronunciation has not been independently scored.

Possible uses
Helps drawing software compensate for input latency, so ink can follow the pen more closely.
Evidence

Not yet established
This is input prediction, not camera motion recognition. File presence does not establish stylus hardware support or activation on MAG1.

03 / Compiled vendor models and companion files

A follow-up read-only check found 31 additional binary candidates that the original extension filter did not include. Some are parts of one network or runtime companions; they are not 31 independently callable AI models. NNA/cadence suffixes do not prove active NPU/DSP use. Sensor names in files do not establish installed camera hardware.

Stereo-depth model parts3 file(s)
Purpose and evidence boundary
Names suggest a multi-part depth-estimation pipeline using stereo views, potentially supporting foreground/background distance separation. Parts 1, 3 and 5 are components, not three complete user-facing models. Actual camera inputs and activation are unverified.
How it is used
Through the matching vendor runtime and configuration. No direct consumer or console operation has been validated for these files.

The frame increases canvas size, not captured scene detail: the framed Ultra res file is not evidence of a 52MP sensor. 50MP is a nominal mode label. Frame rate is measured in fps; the measured average is not a constant-rate guarantee. The published original was recorded without simultaneous screen recording. Portrait playback uses the file rotation metadata.

50MP and 12.5MP: what changes?

Samsung describes the JN1 as a 50MP sensor. Its Tetrapixel design groups four neighboring same-color pixels for a roughly 12.5MP image. High-resolution capture uses remosaic processing. The relationship is approximately 50 ÷ 4 = 12.5; it does not mean four 12.5MP photographs are simply stitched together, or that a finished 12.5MP JPEG is merely enlarged. Samsung ISOCELL JN1.

The existing device evidence identifies s5kjn1. The new capture proves a selectable Ultra res mode and its output dimensions; it does not trace every proprietary ISP stage or prove four times the resolved detail. Bright, steady scenes are better candidates for high-resolution detail; a controlled image-quality comparison remains separate.

Device wallet binding: client-code reference

The installed device-binding app, version 1.2.15, was examined without running a binding operation. Its login path involves a security-chip PIN check; the inspected login and binding paths did not show a Google-account prerequisite. This is a limited code finding, not a guarantee for every service version.

  • The client accepts a wallet address in EVM format. Passing a format check does not verify control of that wallet.
  • The app reads a chip identifier, then requests a fresh challenge from the binding server for that device and address.
  • It signs the challenge-related data through the security chip and verifies the returned data locally.
  • It submits the binding data and signature. The client saves a binding result only after both the HTTP request and the business response succeed; it can later query the server’s current record.
  • No binding, signature or server request was executed. The actual service configuration and reachability, this phone’s binding state and the binding time remain unverified.
  • A displayed binding time can fall back to the phone’s clock when the server omits it. It is not automatically a server activation timestamp. A saved chip identifier also does not establish successful binding.
  • Client error branches cover an already-bound device or address. Server-side one-to-one rules, unbinding and changing the linked wallet still need official confirmation.
  • This client flow does not establish an on-chain registration, warranty start date, node qualification or reward entitlement.

Local call translation and the system voice assistant

Use this chapter to prepare and check the local call translation and the system voice assistant workflow on this firmware.

MAG1WW60-1 · dated captures available

This chapter uses MAG1WW60-1 evidence only. Reference steps are separate from the actions actually recorded.

Quick Settings → call-translation tile

Before you start

MAG1WW60-1 development software; VoiceAssistant 15.00001.22. Use a public automated service or a consented test partner. This session used 10086 automated prompts and did not select a paid service or request an agent.

Recorded MAG1WW60-1 operations

  1. In Quick settings → Edit and sort, locate Translate (VoiceAssistant) and add it if absent. The tile was not in this device’s initial layout.
  2. For the offline-data DEMO, turn off Wi-Fi and mobile data while leaving airplane mode off and cellular voice service available.
  3. Dial the public automated service 10086 using the test SIM. During the call, open Translate and check Chinese → English.
  4. Wait for model loading, then observe newly recognized Chinese speech and English output. Compare the texts; delays and errors can occur.
  5. End the call and restore the original Wi-Fi, mobile-data and shortcut settings.

Controls shown

The screenshots and videos below show the controls used in this session. Capabilities outside their stated scope remain untested.

MAG1WW60-1 observed scope

Translate (VoiceAssistant) is available in the quick-settings edit list on MAG1WW60-1. This screenshot verifies the entry only. MAG1WW60-1 on-device AI DEMO: new Chinese recognition and English output during a 10086 call with Wi-Fi and mobile data disabled. Four network checks passed. Output contains recognition and translation errors; related features are under active development. Silent screen recording. Network controls before the 10086 DEMO. ADB separately verified that both subscriptions had mobile data disabled and there was no default Internet network; cellular voice remained available.

After the test

The call was ended. Wi-Fi, mobile data and the original shortcut layout were restored after capture.

Troubleshooting

  • If the menu differs, record firmware and app versions and use the controls actually shown. Stop when a required credential or accessory is unavailable.

DEMO scope

This is an on-device AI capability DEMO. Related features remain under active, rapid development; output is for reference. Recognition and translation errors were observed. The test does not establish production accuracy, reverse-direction translation, speech synthesis or offline operation of other AI features. Cellular voice still requires the carrier network.

On-device AI capability DEMO

Related features are under active, rapid development. This demonstration shows current on-device capability; results are for reference.

In the 16 October 2026 MAG1WW60-1 test, Wi-Fi and mobile data were off before dialing 10086. New Chinese transcripts and English output appeared during the cellular voice call. ADB checks before, during and after the call confirmed Wi-Fi disabled, mobile data disabled on both subscriptions and no default Internet network. An existing VPN interface remained listed, with no physical Internet connection.

This supports local processing in the tested translation path with its installed models. It does not mean the telephone call itself is offline, or that every AI feature works without Internet access.

  • On MAG1WW60-1 with AI app 15.00001.22, a translation tile was temporarily added for a consented automated-service test call. It was absent from the initial Quick Settings layout, so this is not evidence that every user can find it there by default.

MAGNE, AI and Web3 / ai

On-device AI

Understand the models on MAG1, what they do, and which capabilities have been tested. Explore text, speech and imaging, then follow the desktop-control demonstration.

MAG1WW60-1 · dated captures available

This chapter uses MAG1WW60-1 evidence only. Reference steps are separate from the actions actually recorded.

Installed AI app → Its model and settings (each app requires verification)

Before you start

  • Test prompts without personal information
  • An authorized test account, model and network
  • Check the app prompts for model downloads, installation and any charges

Reference steps · see recorded scope below

  1. gptos.intelligence.assistant 2.1.570 was found as a user-installed package. Its presence does not establish that it is factory-installed MAGNE AI.
  2. Inventory each AI app in actual use separately, including sign-in, input, voice, images, model selection, history, files, permissions and account deletion.
  3. Test text input and results using a prompt without personal information. If an account is required, pause only that app's test.
  4. Verify offline capability per application, with model identity, network conditions, fresh output and network restoration recorded. Completed console and call-translation demonstrations are scoped below.
  5. Voice and image features involve microphone/camera permissions and uploads. Establish where processing occurs and the service conditions.
  6. Check generated results for accuracy and limitations. Model output is not official evidence of device specifications.

Buttons and options

Button / optionPurpose and limits
Model selectionA model name does not prove that it runs locally
HistoryMay contain personal information; not captured in the recorded demonstration
Voice / imagesPermissions and upload routes require separate verification
OfflineRequires evidence from testing without a network connection

MAG1WW60-1 observed scope

MAG1WW60-1 integrates dedicated camera visual-AI components and a separate local call-translation model path. The camera application and JN1 configuration contain scene-recognition, denoising, depth/segmentation and beauty components. Integration does not establish that every component executes in every mode.

In the MAG1WW60-1 call-translation test, the Qwen2.5-1.5B model service opened the NPU device and completed task counts increased after translation was enabled. This supports NPU use by that translation path. A subsequent DEMO produced new transcripts and translations with Wi-Fi and mobile data disabled; see the recorded test conditions below. The processor used by each ASR/TTS stage was not established.

Camera mode-by-mode runtime tracing remains pending. There is no current evidence that ordinary photography uses the translation language model, or that CPU, GPU and NPU simultaneously execute the same model.

MAGNE.AI x FIH · DESKTOP DEMO

On-device AI · Control MAG1 from your computer

This engineering console sends requests over local HTTP and USB / ADB to the connected MAG1, then displays the phone’s response. It is a development demonstration, not a preinstalled consumer app. Features continue to evolve.

MAG1WW60-1 · Android 15 · 2026-10-16 · UTC+08:00 · English interface

Computer→ USB / ADB →MAG1→Results on the computer

Watch a real request

Connection check → ASR transcription → independent TTS synthesis → playback. The overview contains saved results; the video then submits fresh requests.

Real browser frames are sampled in chronological order and held until the next frame; this is not a smooth, frame-complete screen recording. Use the returned metrics, not video duration, for timing. The playback soundtrack is this run’s generated WAV aligned with the Play action, not a room-microphone recording.

Open / download the video · Capture record and file hashes

Follow the workflow

  1. Connect the prepared MAG1 by USB, complete normal device authorization, start the local console, and choose English or Traditional Chinese.
  2. Select Check connection. Confirm MAG1WW60-1 and the required service state before testing.
  3. In Speech recognition, query languages and select Transcribe sample. Compare the returned text with “The weather is sunny today.” This tests a synthetic file, not live microphone capture.
  4. In Speech synthesis, choose the sample text, matching voice and speed; select Generate on phone. After success, play or download the WAV and review any warnings.
  5. Use Installed models to read each file’s purpose and evidence. File presence alone does not confirm active inference or acceleration.

Two separate execution paths

ModuleTested path and boundary
ASRMAGNE.AI x FIH service via Android Binder. The English sample returned a transcript. This does not establish every language or the accelerator used.
Kokoro TTSIndependent sherpa-onnx runtime on phone CPU, two threads. This demonstration does not invoke or repair the FIH TTS service, whose model-path mismatch remains.
GemmaSeparate model/runtime experiments are outside this recording; they are not presented as FIH SDK support.
What this recording establishes

The computer can control these prepared phone-side test paths and display real responses. Wi-Fi and mobile data remained enabled in this recording; it is not a new network-isolation test. The separately recorded offline call-translation demo below has its own conditions.

Screenshots you can inspect

Listen to this run’s output

Hello. This speech is generated locally on the MAG1 phone.

Audio 4.26 s · synthesis 9.45 s · RTF 2.22. Synthesis excludes model loading, USB transfer and playback. A single observation, not a benchmark average. Unknown-token / skipped-phoneme warnings were returned; pronunciation has not been independently scored.

This manual embeds static evidence. It does not connect visitors to the local control service. Running a test requires the prepared computer, console environment and an authorized MAG1 USB connection.

MAG1 · ON-DEVICE AI

On-device AI model guide

This covers every model-format file identified in the dated scan, additional compiled vendor candidates, and the separately installed Gemma experiment. It is not a claim that all models on the phone have been found: private app data, other APK archives and unrecognized proprietary formats remain outside the scan.

5AI service model files
11System / vendor model files
31Compiled candidates / companions
1Separately installed Gemma model

MAG1WW60-1 · 2026-10-16 · Counts are files or explicitly identified model artifacts, not independent capabilities. File size is storage size, not runtime RAM usage.

Language & speechSystem & visionCompiled vendor filesIndependent Gemma

A conceptual voice workflow is VAD → ASR → LLM → TTS: detect speech, transcribe it, generate or translate text, then speak it. This explains how the roles fit together; it does not claim that every MAG1 app uses all these exact files.

01 / Language and speech

Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct · UNIText generation and LLM translation
Input → output
Text prompt → generated text. Translation uses the same language model.
What it is for
Short answers, supplied-text summaries, drafting and translation. Generated facts still need checking.
How to use it
Console: Text generation or Text translation, using EDGE_ONLY. These controls call the firmware service; they do not offer arbitrary model-file replacement.
Recorded status and limits
Real text and translation service responses were recorded. The service code selects this UNI model path. Accelerator observations from the separate call-translation test do not prove the backend of every console request.
/product/media/models/llm/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-UNI/Qwen2.5-1.5B-a16w8-feo.unillm1,950.85 MiB
Paraformer · INT8Automatic speech recognition (ASR)
Input → output
Speech audio → a written transcript. It does not generate speech or translate by itself.
What it is for
Turn spoken words into text for dictation, captions or a later translation step. These are possible uses, not all verified product integrations.
How to use it
Console: Speech recognition → Query languages → Transcribe sample. The console currently tests the service, not a user-selectable Paraformer backend.
Recorded status and limits
The installed file is referenced in ASR code. The English sample returned text, but runtime tracing has not identified which ASR model handled it. The exposed service reports zh-CN and en-US.

SenseVoice · INT8Alternative speech-recognition model
Input → output
Speech audio → text through an alternative ASR configuration.
What it is for
An alternative recognition path when the application and runtime select the matching configuration.
How to use it
No independent model selector or dedicated SenseVoice test is exposed in the current console. Testing it separately requires a verified configuration or dedicated test program.
Recorded status and limits
The file and code reference are present; independent inference is untested. The zh-en-ja-ko-yue folder name does not establish Japanese, Korean or Cantonese support in the exposed service, nor other SenseVoice capabilities.

Silero VADVoice activity detection
Input → output
Audio segments → whether speech is present, helping identify speech start and end.
What it is for
Avoid sending long silences to ASR and divide speech into usable segments. VAD does not transcribe words or identify the speaker.
How to use it
A supporting stage inside the recognition pipeline, not a separate consumer app or current console button.
Recorded status and limits
ASR voice-activity code references this file. Endpoint accuracy and an independent VAD run have not been tested.

Kokoro · multilingual v1.1Text-to-speech synthesis (TTS)
Input → output
Text + voice + speed → a speech waveform, saved here as WAV.
What it is for
Read answers, passages or translated text aloud. This complements ASR: one listens, the other speaks.
How to use it
Console: Speech synthesis → choose a matching voice → Generate on phone → Play / Download WAV. The demonstrated path is independent sherpa-onnx on phone CPU, two threads.
Recorded status and limits
English and Chinese WAV outputs were recorded. Original FIH TTS still expects model.int8.onnx, while model.onnx is installed. Independent success does not repair that mismatch. Runtime token/phoneme warnings remain; pronunciation has not been independently scored.

Helps drawing software compensate for input latency, so ink can follow the pen more closely.

Model
Gemma 3n E2B IT · INT4 · LiteRT-LM
Purpose
A generative model for local text interaction and, when image support is enabled in the matching app, image questions. It is separate from camera depth, denoising and segmentation models.
How to use it
Google AI Edge Gallery → imported model → text chat or the image-enabled import → select a permitted picture and ask a short question. It is not a selectable FIH model in the current console.
Recorded evidence
English and Traditional Chinese text outputs, a three-run 64-input/64-output-token benchmark, and one image description were completed on MAG1WW60-1. Gallery 1.0.20 labels the LLM backend CPU; the image test logs also contain OpenCL activity, so the entire vision path is not claimed to be CPU-only.
Measured example
Gallery reported an average decode rate of 2.11 tokens/s across three runs. This is not directly comparable to Qwen/FIH because model, tokenizer, runtime and workload differ.
Limits and counting
The image-enabled import is a byte-identical copy of the same model, counted once. This does not establish FIH compatibility, NPU acceleration, real-time camera integration, audio support, long-context stability or general visual accuracy.
gemma-3n-E2B-it-int4.litertlm3,486.47 MiB

What is not counted as another model

  • LLM-based translation reuses Qwen. Gemma text and image imports reuse the same model artifact. Network parts and network/cadence pairs may belong to one processing pipeline.

  • Gemini is described in its own chapter. An installed app or NPU driver is not proof of a locally installed Gemini model. Camera AI libraries without identified model files are components, not additional named models in this register.

On-device AI capability DEMO

Related features are under active, rapid development. This demonstration shows current on-device capability; results are for reference.

In the 16 October 2026 MAG1WW60-1 test, Wi-Fi and mobile data were off before dialing 10086. New Chinese transcripts and English output appeared during the cellular voice call. ADB checks before, during and after the call confirmed Wi-Fi disabled, mobile data disabled on both subscriptions and no default Internet network. An existing VPN interface remained listed, with no physical Internet connection.

This supports local processing in the tested translation path with its installed models. It does not mean the telephone call itself is offline, or that every AI feature works without Internet access.

MAG1WW60-1 local AI: current evidence

MAG1WW60-1 integrates dedicated camera visual-AI components and a separate local call-translation model path. The camera application and JN1 configuration contain scene-recognition, denoising, depth/segmentation and beauty components. Integration does not establish that every component executes in every mode.

In the MAG1WW60-1 call-translation test, the Qwen2.5-1.5B model service opened the NPU device and completed task counts increased after translation was enabled. This supports NPU use by that translation path. A subsequent DEMO produced new transcripts and translations with Wi-Fi and mobile data disabled; see the recorded test conditions below. The processor used by each ASR/TTS stage was not established.

Camera mode-by-mode runtime tracing remains pending. There is no current evidence that ordinary photography uses the translation language model, or that CPU, GPU and NPU simultaneously execute the same model.

Reference steps · see recorded scope below

  1. Prepare a non-private test scene before opening the camera. Choose a scene without private information.
  2. Inventory the actual controls for photo, video, front/rear switching, zoom, flash, timer, grid, aspect ratio, resolution and storage location.
  3. In video mode, verify available combinations of resolution, frame rate, HDR and stabilization, then record a test clip and inspect its file properties.

Limits and versions

The official site lists rear video up to 4K30, front video up to FHD30, HDR and EIS. The dated sample below confirms a rear 4K capture; front FHD30 and HDR/EIS combinations were not retested in this batch.

See the recorded scope and limitations on this page.

MAG1WW60-1 development software. Evidence covers only the dated captures and explicitly described tests.

4K video, Ultra res photos and native watermark

Captured on MAG1WW60-1 on 16 October 2026. These are camera output files, separate from the 720 × 1592 screen recordings used to show controls. Photos retain the camera-generated black Frame watermark. No website watermark or image enhancement has been added.

ModeBefore FramePublished file / result
Capture3072 × 4080 · 12.53MP3072 × 4416 · includes black frame
More → Ultra res6144 × 8064 · 49.55MP6144 × 8432 · includes black frame
Video → UHD 4K, 30fps3840 × 2160 · HEVC250 frames / 8.296 s ≈ 30.13 fps average; silent

The frame increases canvas size, not captured scene detail: the framed Ultra res file is not evidence of a 52MP sensor. 50MP is a nominal mode label. Frame rate is measured in fps; the measured average is not a constant-rate guarantee. The published original was recorded without simultaneous screen recording. Portrait playback uses the file rotation metadata.

50MP and 12.5MP: what changes?

Samsung describes the JN1 as a 50MP sensor. Its Tetrapixel design groups four neighboring same-color pixels for a roughly 12.5MP image. High-resolution capture uses remosaic processing. The relationship is approximately 50 ÷ 4 = 12.5; it does not mean four 12.5MP photographs are simply stitched together, or that a finished 12.5MP JPEG is merely enlarged. Samsung ISOCELL JN1.

The existing device evidence identifies s5kjn1. The new capture proves a selectable Ultra res mode and its output dimensions; it does not trace every proprietary ISP stage or prove four times the resolved detail. Bright, steady scenes are better candidates for high-resolution detail; a controlled image-quality comparison remains separate.

Camera controls and watermark behavior

  1. Video → Settings → Video size(Back camera) → UHD 4K, 30fps; return and use the red shutter to start/stop.
  2. More → Ultra res → Shutter; this is the high-resolution photo mode.
  3. Capture → Settings → Picture Watermark → CUSTOMIZED → enable Frame watermark → Background: Black.
  4. UNIVERSAL → Customize watermark provides custom text such as MAGNE.AI. On this build, enabling Frame changed that setting to No; the black frame displays MAG1 plus exposure data.
  5. No video-watermark control was found in the tested Video settings. The 4K sample has no native watermark.

File metadata and SHA-256 verification

MAG1WW60-1 screenshots and recordings · 16 October 2026

These captures confirm only the visible screens and actions shown on this development build. They do not verify every setting, external accessory or end-to-end feature. Android touch markers show ADB-injected input; the native coordinate strip is retained. No app icons are masked.

Current capture status

See the dated MAG1WW60-1 screenshots and recordings above.

16 October supplement · MAG1WW60-1 development software

  • MAG1WW60-1, camera 1.0000.19: the recorded test saved one 4080 × 3072 JPEG and a 31.89 s, 1920 × 1080 H.264 video at about 30 fps. Complete file decoding and device/computer hashes passed. Front/rear previews switched successfully; no front photo was saved.
  • A later 16 October capture confirmed More → Ultra res and a 6144 × 8064 image (49.55MP) before adding the Frame watermark. The earlier 12.53MP sample alone did not establish this mode. Front-camera driver naming and public output dimensions likewise describe different layers.
  • A camera-app freezer/Binder exit occurred before the successful capture. It is a recorded issue for investigation, not proof that a sensor or AI algorithm failed. Long recordings, 4K/HDR/EIS combinations, night/portrait/macro and image-quality improvement remain untested here.

Evidence sources: functional · camera-ai

MAG1WW60-1 camera visual AI and image processing

MAG1WW60-1 has camera-specific visual-AI components. Current static evidence identifies scene-recognition control/result paths, AI single/multi-frame denoising libraries and JN1 configuration, plus depth, segmentation, beauty and focus-related components. Their presence and configuration do not prove activation in each photo or 4K frame.

Conceptual photo path: sensor capture → RAW data → ISP image processing and exposure/white-balance/focus control → mode-dependent denoising, HDR or visual AI → image encoding. Branches and processing order depend on the mode; this is not a recovered proprietary pipeline.

Video continuously captures frames, processes them and encodes the selected output. The published MAG1WW60-1 4K sample confirms resolution and file output, not simultaneous HDR, stabilization and NPU acceleration. Current video-AI trigger conditions remain unverified.

Recognize charging status and investigate heat or slow charging. A rated maximum does not mean every session reaches that power.

USB-C / compatible wireless charger → Settings → Battery

Before you start

  • Compatible, undamaged charger, cable or wireless charging pad
  • Dry device and ports
  • Remove metal objects and incompatible cases before wireless charging

Reference steps · see recorded scope below

  1. Wired: connect an undamaged cable to USB-C and a compatible charger, then check for the on-screen charging indicator.
  2. Wireless: align the center of the phone’s back as directed by the charging-pad instructions, keep it in contact and check for charging status. The alignment position has not been tested.
  3. Open Settings → Battery, note the charge level and status, then check later whether the charge level increases.
  4. Stop charging if there is overheating, an unusual smell, swelling, liquid ingress or port damage, and contact a qualified repair service.
  5. When finished, unplug by holding the connector rather than pulling the cable. Lift the phone off the pad to end wireless charging.

Power on → Android setup wizard

Before you start

  • Sufficient battery charge and dry ports
  • A working network; your Google account if you choose account-based services, and the original credentials if ownership verification is requested
  • The current test device is already initialized; reproducing the wizard would require a reset

Reference steps · see recorded scope below

  1. Use the power button to start the phone. Follow the supplied instructions for how long to hold it; no unverified duration is specified here.
  2. Choose a language and region on the welcome screen, then follow the on-screen instructions.
  3. Connect to your own Wi-Fi or SIM data as prompted. Complete any network sign-in if required.
  4. Review account, data-transfer, service and permission choices. Copying data from an old phone is the user’s decision; Skip is not a mandatory choice.
  5. The owner should enter the screen lock directly on the device. Do not record or share the password.
  6. After reaching the home screen, check the system and bundled app versions, then follow the quick start for everyday settings.

Three separate processes

ProcessMeaning and limits
Android initial setupLanguage, network and account choices before normal use. Completing setup does not establish a warranty date or node eligibility.
Factory reset protection (FRP)Ownership verification associated with a protected device after reset. It is separate from ordinary new-device account choices.
MAGNE device wallet bindingAn independent app-and-server binding flow. See the client-code reference below; it has not been executed in the recorded demonstration.

Device wallet binding: client-code reference →

Google account choices and reset protection

MAG1 uses a Google setup wizard. The installed version contains a path for skipping account setup. Follow the choices actually shown on your phone: the visible path depends on device state, configuration and later manufacturer checks. This is not proof that every first-boot scenario can skip an account, or that the flow is identical to a Pixel.

If reset protection requests ownership verification, use the original credentials required by the on-screen prompt. This phone’s current FRP state was not established by the read-only audit.

The available diagnostic query was blocked by system permissions. Missing settings or empty output do not prove protection is off. Ask the manufacturer for an official read-only status report if confirmation is needed; repeating USB authorization is not a solution to this restriction.

This chapter uses MAG1WW60-1 evidence only. Reference steps are separate from the actions actually recorded.

Device and packaging → Official MAG1 specifications

Before you start

  • Have the phone and packing list ready
  • Keep ports dry
  • Do not insert the SIM eject tool into a microphone opening

Reference steps · see recorded scope below

  1. Compare the package label—model MA1, product MAG1—with the order. Do not publish the IMEI or serial number.
  2. Identify the USB-C port, 3.5 mm headphone jack, SIM tray, cameras and side buttons. Their exact positions still require an annotated hardware check; do not insert an eject tool based on a guess.
  3. Check the packing list for the phone, cable, charger, SIM eject tool and any NFC accessories. A feature listed on the website does not mean its accessory is included in every shipment.
  4. Identify the power and volume buttons from the device markings. Short presses, long presses and button combinations each need verification on this model.
  5. Remove transport protection before first use. Check the glass, ports and accessories for damage; contact the seller if anything is damaged.

MAG1WW60-1 observed scope

Dated ADB hardware and driver observations are available below, alongside an attributed T9100 product sheet. Exterior and packaging photography remains unavailable; technical tables do not replace physical inspection.

Cancel, exit and restore

If accessories do not match, stop connecting them. Keep the packaging and order details and contact official support.

  • Eject tool does not fit: first confirm the SIM-tray opening; do not force it

Limits and versions

Website specifications are manufacturer information. No external-camera footage was captured; a screen recording cannot verify physical handling.

See the recorded scope and limitations on this page.

MAG1WW60-1 development software. Evidence covers only the dated captures and explicitly described tests.

Current capture status

No usable current-build capture yet. Missing material is listed in the coverage ledger; no other firmware capture is substituted.

16 October supplement · MAG1WW60-1 development software

  • The sample reports a 12 GB RAM class; Linux exposes about 11.14 GiB. Approximately 6.91 GiB of zram is compressed swap, not extra physical RAM.
  • The storage device identifies as WDC SDINFDO4-512G and reports UFS 3.1. Its main block device is about 512.083 GB; /data is about 464.00 GiB before considering used space. These are different units and allocation layers, not a throughput benchmark.
  • The display interface reports 1080 × 2388 and 60/120 Hz modes. The 60 Hz snapshot does not remove the separately observed 120 Hz mode. HDR types are declared capabilities, not measured brightness or certification.
  • This sample has no verified Type-C display output or working ToF ranging. A VL53L0 device object is unbound; the DP transmitter and PTN38003A redriver nodes are disabled. Node presence is not an accessory compatibility result.
  • UMP9620 audio-codec binding supersedes the inference from the legacy sc2730 sound-card name. The wireless-charger names CPS4021/CPS4201 differ and still require BOM confirmation. Exact component models are not substituted for functional tests.

Evidence sources: hardware · drivers · usb-typec · system · tee

T9100 platform specifications and MAG1 evidence

The following specifications are attributed to a user-supplied, UNISOC-branded T9100 product sheet (one page), reviewed on 16 October 2026. They describe platform capabilities, separately from the device observations below.

ItemUser-supplied product sheetInterpretation for MAG1WW60-1
CPU / process8 cores: 1× Cortex-A76 at 2.7 GHz + 3× Cortex-A76 at 2.3 GHz + 4× Cortex-A55 at 2.1 GHz; 6 nm.Driver frequency limits below are a separate observation. In particular, the small-core limit reported by this device is 2.184 GHz; it is not silently substituted for the sheet’s 2.1 GHz.
GPUArm Mali-G57, 4 cores.The device reports Mali-G57. The four-core specification comes from this sheet, not an independent on-device core-count measurement.
NPU / VDSPNPU: 8.0 TOPS; VDSP: VQ7.The sheet does not state the precision or measurement conditions for TOPS. This is a platform rating, not measured MAG1 application throughput, and does not support a 10 TOPS claim.
Camera / ISPVivimagic 6.0; four-core ISP (2 main + 2 auxiliary); up to 108 MP. AI denoising, bokeh, beauty and face detection are listed.The MAG1 camera’s demonstrated modes and output sizes remain the device evidence. Platform support does not establish that every visual-AI function is enabled in MAG1WW60-1.
Video / display4K 60 fps encoding; 4K 60 fps, 10-bit decoding. FHD+ 120 fps or QHD+ 60 fps display support.These are chip capabilities. Keep the demonstrated MAG1 4K 30 fps workflow and actual display modes separately documented; do not relabel them as 4K 60 fps or a QHD+ panel.
Memory / storageLPDDR4X 2133 MHz, up to 32 GB; eMMC 5.1 / UFS 3.1 support.Platform limits and supported interfaces do not establish the installed capacity or storage component of this MAG1.
SecurityiSE solution, trusted execution environment and hardware cryptographic engine.The sheet does not identify MAG1’s discrete SE part number, COS, applets or certification scope. Keep the eSE/OMAPI and Trusty observations below separate.

Source and scope →

CPU / GPU / NPU — detected capabilities and runtime evidence

Evidence collected on 16 October 2026, MAG1WW60-1 development software (system build MAG1WW60-1). Frequency tables, driver readings and application execution are separate observations.

ProcessorDetected informationHow to interpret it
CPU8 cores; 3 cpufreq policy groups. CPU0–3: 2.184 GHz; CPU4–6: 2.301 GHz; CPU7: 2.704 GHz. Governor: uscfreq.These are cpuinfo_max frequency limits reported by the driver, not sustained all-core clocks or benchmark results.
GPUMali-G57; OpenGL ES 3.2. Driver: mali. Reported devfreq levels: 384 / 512 / 680 / 850 MHz.The initial scan sampled 384 MHz; the later translation test sampled 384, 680 and 850 MHz. Rendering also uses the GPU; these readings do not prove AI GPU execution.
NPUDevice-tree identifier: img,ax3xxx-nna. Bound driver: ax3xxx-nna. Reported levels: 307.2 / 384 / 500 / 614.4 / 768 / 1000 MHz.The translation test reported devfreq cur_freq / target_freq of 307.2 MHz throughout 177 samples. debugfs core_freq_khz remained 30000 and disagreed with devfreq; the physical clock needs vendor clarification. The 1 GHz entry is a listed level, not a measured operating peak.

What has run on the NPU?

Local call translation has direct NPU execution evidence: enabling translation increased driver task counters, while the LLM service held /dev/vha0 open and mapped Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-UNI. The user confirmed translation output. The second run added 15,121 completed tasks including tail processing; tasks are not tokens, and cumulative execution time is not user-perceived latency.

The initial driver study did not isolate Internet access. A later 10086 DEMO produced new Chinese recognition and English translation with Wi-Fi and mobile data disabled. That supports the tested local translation path; it does not establish measured TOPS, tokens/s, NPU clock calibration, GPU AI execution or joint CPU/GPU/NPU execution of the same model. CPU architecture and GPU core count are now separately sourced from the product sheet above. View the recorded DEMO →

Sources: system · drivers · functional

SE — secure element, wallet interfaces and verification limits

Evidence dated 16 October 2026: MAG1WW60-1 development software, system build MAG1WW60-1; wallet USERDEBUG 1.2.15. The service observations and static code findings below are distinct from successful wallet transactions.

ItemObserved evidenceInterpretation and limits
SE availabilityThe system scan reported eSE1 with mIsConnected=true. Android OMAPI ISecureElementService / com.android.se and android.hardware.secure_element@1.2-service.hed were running.This confirms reported connectivity and the service chain, not successful execution of every wallet operation. The HAL interface version 1.2 is not a COS version.
Wallet integrationThe app uses Android OMAPI SEService / Reader / Session / Channel and the HED OSU SDK (OSU-SDK-1.2.3).Static paths include PIN verification, seed/mnemonic generation and import, public-key retrieval and signing. The audit did not execute APDU commands, create/import a wallet or sign/broadcast transactions.
COS and appletsThe SDK provides COS-version query, upgrade and recovery APIs; wallet code references seed and coin applets.The current COS version and installed applet inventory were not queried. APIs in the APK do not establish the state or security properties of the chip firmware.
Exact chip specificationsHED service names and the hednfc binding are available as integration evidence.The exact SE part number, CPU architecture, physical clock, memory capacity and EAL certification remain unverified. CIU98M50, SC300 or 120 MHz must not be presented as detected device specifications without matching vendor evidence.
TEE and PIN protectionThe separate platform TEE reports Unisoc Trusty v2.1.1. Wallet code requests AndroidKeyStore AES/GCM protection for a saved PIN with user authentication.Trusty v2.1.1 is not the SE COS version. The specific key securityLevel and hardware backing were not attested; the entire Android wallet must not be described as executing in the TEE.
StrongBox and NFC backupStrongBox was not declared in the inspected feature list. NFC backup uses a separate external card.Missing StrongBox declaration does not disprove an SE, and does not establish where a particular Keystore key resides. The external backup card, embedded SE and platform TEE are distinct components.

How it fits into the wallet

Wallet signing path in code: Android transaction preparation and confirmation → OMAPI / HED SE HAL → embedded SE and wallet applet → Android assembles and broadcasts the signed transaction. PIN protection follows a separate AndroidKeyStore / KeyMint platform-service path.

The app handles mnemonic plaintext for display/import/backup, so the current implementation does not support the claim that a mnemonic never leaves the secure element. Neither SE-backed trusted transaction display nor private-key non-exportability was established by this audit. A functioning SE service also does not certify the security of the Android app. See the wallet chapter for the development-build review status.

Vendor evidence still needed: matching part number/BOM and certificate scope; COS and applet versions; key-export boundaries; PIN retry/lockout behavior; firmware signature verification and anti-rollback; and trusted input/display design. This section publishes no device serials, APDU payloads, PINs, mnemonics or private keys.

Sources: system · wallet-structure · wallet-build · tee

Snapshot: 16 October 2026 · MAG1WW60-1 development software · system build MAG1WW60-1 · Android 15 / userdebug · kernel 5.15.170-android13-8-g123978c57a69-ab215.

MAGNE, AI and Web3 / mag-wallet

MAGNE Wallet: versions, networks and safe preparation

Blockchain network support

MAGNE Wallet’s supported blockchain network list will continue to be updated, with more networks added over time. MHASH L2 and the MAGNE L1 testnet have already been added to the supported network list. Please refer to the network list in the latest wallet version for current availability.

Check the installed build and network before using a wallet. The current 1.2.15 analysis identifies implemented paths and limitations; it is not a completed transaction test or a production security approval.

MAG1WW60-1 · dated captures available

This chapter uses MAG1WW60-1 evidence only. Reference steps are separate from the actions actually recorded.

Manage wallet → Add wallet → review choices → close; creation and financial operations remain untested.

Before you start

  • This analyzed build is for controlled testing pending engineering fixes and re-verification; do not treat it as approved for real-asset use.
  • No test-wallet creation, import, signing, transfer or NFC recovery was performed in this integration.
  • Required conditions include the correct app/firmware, a compatible NFC card for card workflows, and camera permission for scanning.

Wallet 1.2.15 interface check · 16 October 2026

In the sampled Private space profile, Manage wallet displayed No wallet. The new recording opens Add wallet, shows Create new wallet, Restore wallet and Import mnemonics, then closes the menu. No option was executed. These are English-UI entry demonstrations only; no addresses, balances, recovery phrases or PIN entry are included. Creation, recovery, signing, transfers and card compatibility remain unverified by this capture.

Reference steps · see recorded scope below

  1. Check the phone firmware and the wallet package/version first. The 16 October sample is MAG1WW60-1 userdebug with com.magicalhash.wallet 1.2.15; its underlying factory package is 1.2.14. The USER and USERDEBUG packages share code but have different signatures.
  2. Creation, phrase import, account management, PIN changes and NFC backup/restore have code paths. Their exact screens and button sequence still need verification on this build; no successful creation or restoration is claimed here.
  3. Before any future test, confirm that the wallet has no real assets, identify the network and compatible card, and keep recovery phrases, private keys and PIN entry out of screenshots and recordings.
  4. Review the network table below. A testnet flag does not force every network to a testnet, and a token ticker is not enough to identify the network.
  5. Use only the connection and authorization details actually shown by the app. Inspect the DApp origin, requested network, signing account and amount; cancel unexpected requests. Do not interpret a connection or a risk message as a successful or safe transaction.

Functions found in code

FunctionEvidence and limits
Create / import / manageThe empty Manage wallet page and Add wallet choices are captured; creation, import, restoration and capacity limits remain untested.
Receive / send / historyCode exists; balances, fees, signing and broadcast must be tested per network.
PIN / biometricsBiometric login requests Android Keystore protection for a stored PIN. Biometric availability and signing fallback behavior still need engineering clarification.
NFC backup / restoreRequires a supported external card, password and recovery test. Card model, capacity, retry/lockout and cross-device recovery are unverified.
DApp / WalletConnectWebView bridge and session logic exist; initial approved chains are restricted below.
NFT asset pageDisplays “developing”. ERC721 decoding does not establish a working NFT portfolio.

MAG1WW60-1 observed scope

In the sampled Private space profile, Manage wallet displayed No wallet. The new recording opens Add wallet, shows Create new wallet, Restore wallet and Import mnemonics, then closes the menu. No option was executed. These are English-UI entry demonstrations only; no addresses, balances, recovery phrases or PIN entry are included. Creation, recovery, signing, transfers and card compatibility remain unverified by this capture.

Cancel, exit and restore

Go back or cancel authentication. Creation, import, recovery and transactions were not performed. Do not clear wallet data.

Troubleshooting

  • Scan does not open: check camera permission for the active user. The sampled user had not granted it; this is not proof that scanning is absent.
  • Network or balance differs: verify mainnet/testnet, exact network ID and RPC. MAGNE/MHASH configurations are testnets; USE_TESTNET does not apply uniformly.
  • WalletConnect rejects a chain: compare the DApp request with the initial approved chain list; custom-network support still needs integration testing.
  • Biometrics unavailable: cancel a sensitive operation and seek supported authentication guidance. Do not assume every signing path always forces a second fingerprint check.
  • NFC recovery fails: confirm card compatibility and backup version; do not overwrite the only backup or clear wallet data.
  • NFT page is empty: the analyzed asset tab is still marked developing.

Limits and versions

Static analysis found unresolved security issues. USER and USERDEBUG 1.2.15 share the relevant code; changing the signature alone is not a fix. SE participation does not make the whole Android app a trusted environment. No user-data leak or remote asset theft was demonstrated. Engineering fixes and asset-free re-testing are required before a production-use judgment.

The project statement “one HD set + 255 software wallets” and the code constants of 20 wallet indices / 100 accounts describe different concepts. Neither is used here as a verified SE capacity or as a replacement for the other; vendor mapping and boundary testing are pending.

MAG1WW60-1 development software. Evidence covers only the dated captures and explicitly described tests.

Three separate processes

Read about initial setup, reset protection and device binding →

Network coverage: configuration is not a passed transfer test

16 labels and 24 configured network entries were found. Mainnet/testnet entries are counted separately. Non-EVM configured IDs are app identifiers, not universally EVM chain IDs. No end-to-end chain test was performed.

LabelConfigured networksCurrent evidence / limit
BTCBitcoin mainnet / testnetUTXO handler; untested
ETHEthereum / SepoliaEVM path; untested
BNBBSC 56 / testnet 97Default coin mapping selects mainnet
MAGNE20250810Testnet configuration
MHASH20250827Testnet; MHA mainnet/testnet aliases both resolve here
SOLSolana mainnet / testnetHandler; untested
DOGEDogecoin mainnetHandler; untested
LTCLitecoin mainnetHandler; untested
ADACardano mainnet / PreprodHandler; untested
XRPXRP Ledger mainnet / testnetHandler; untested
DOTPolkadot mainnet / PaseoHandler; untested

WalletConnect initially approves Ethereum (1), Sepolia (11155111), BSC (56), BSC testnet (97) and Polygon (137), all eip155 namespaces. Its 23 declared methods are not 23 passed compatibility tests. This is not 16-chain WalletConnect support; non-EVM sessions and custom-chain negotiation are unverified.

Evidence sources: wallet-structure · wallet-build

SE, TEE and the NFC card have different roles

Wallet signing code calls OMAPI / HED SE interfaces. Biometric PIN protection uses Android Keystore / KeyMint, with Trusty services present. The NFC backup card is an external device. Android still handles transaction construction, confirmation, networking and decrypted recovery phrases during display/backup; “the recovery phrase never leaves the SE” is not supported. No independent trusted transaction display, exact SE model, certification, retry policy or anti-rollback behavior was established.

Evidence sources: wallet-structure · tee

This chapter uses MAG1WW60-1 evidence only. Reference steps are separate from the actions actually recorded.

Device wallet binding: client-code reference

The installed device-binding app, version 1.2.15, was examined without running a binding operation. Its login path involves a security-chip PIN check; the inspected login and binding paths did not show a Google-account prerequisite. This is a limited code finding, not a guarantee for every service version.

  • The client accepts a wallet address in EVM format. Passing a format check does not verify control of that wallet.
  • The app reads a chip identifier, then requests a fresh challenge from the binding server for that device and address.
  • It signs the challenge-related data through the security chip and verifies the returned data locally.
  • It submits the binding data and signature. The client saves a binding result only after both the HTTP request and the business response succeed; it can later query the server’s current record.
  • No binding, signature or server request was executed. The actual service configuration and reachability, this phone’s binding state and the binding time remain unverified.
  • A displayed binding time can fall back to the phone’s clock when the server omits it. It is not automatically a server activation timestamp. A saved chip identifier also does not establish successful binding.
  • Client error branches cover an already-bound device or address. Server-side one-to-one rules, unbinding and changing the linked wallet still need official confirmation.
  • This client flow does not establish an on-chain registration, warranty start date, node qualification or reward entitlement.

Read about initial setup, reset protection and device binding →

TROUBLESHOOTING / Diagnose an issue

Find the cause.
Change one thing.

Record the time, version, error message and reproduction steps. Stop before authentication, payment, deletion or reset. Clearing data should not be the first step.

SymptomFirst checksRelated steps
No internet connectionCheck airplane mode and Internet first, then SIM, VPN, DNS and captive-portal sign-in. Change one item at a time.Open guide →
Delayed notificationsCheck app notifications → channels → Do Not Disturb → Battery startup/lock-screen restrictions → network.Open guide →
Screen hard to read or turns off quicklyCheck brightness, adaptive brightness, Screen timeout and accessibility display options under Display.Open guide →
Unexpected sound or vibrationDistinguish media, calls, ringtones, notifications and alarms; check headphone output and Do Not Disturb.Open guide →
USB only chargesCheck the data cable, device unlock, USB purpose and computer recognition. A charging-only cable cannot transfer data.Open guide →
Bluetooth device not foundPut the accessory in pairing mode and check distance and identity. Cancel immediately if pairing codes differ.Open guide →
Insufficient storageInspect Storage categories first, then handle only content with verified backups. Do not clear wallet data.Open guide →
Wallet will not open or recovery failsPreserve data and check the package and version. Stop before confirmation if a test account or authentication is unavailable.Open guide →
Different system versionCompare the actual build and region and recheck entries. Update installation and firmware flashing have not been tested.Open guide →
Liquid ingress, damage or abnormal heatStop use and charging and contact official support. Current specifications do not promise immersion protection.Open guide →

Before contacting support

  • Product model and build; app name, package and version.
  • Error text, time, network/accessory conditions and the shortest reproduction steps.
  • Screenshots without personal data; share necessary order details only through private official channels.
  • Do not send private keys, recovery phrases, passwords or verification codes, or publish personal identification.

The official Contact page lists official@magne.ai for product support. No external message was sent. Warranty duration and service terms await a formal policy.

Wallet, connection and permission checks

  • Scan does not open: check camera permission for the active user. The sampled user had not granted it; this is not proof that scanning is absent.
  • Network or balance differs: verify mainnet/testnet, exact network ID and RPC. MAGNE/MHASH configurations are testnets; USE_TESTNET does not apply uniformly.
  • WalletConnect rejects a chain: compare the DApp request with the initial approved chain list; custom-network support still needs integration testing.
  • Biometrics unavailable: cancel a sensitive operation and seek supported authentication guidance. Do not assume every signing path always forces a second fingerprint check.
  • NFC recovery fails: confirm card compatibility and backup version; do not overwrite the only backup or clear wallet data.
  • NFT page is empty: the analyzed asset tab is still marked developing.

Wallet limits →

Build-specific issues

  • The MAG1WW60-1 camera test recorded a freezer/Binder exit before successful capture. Record the time, app/build and visible symptoms; it is not established as an AI or sensor fault.
  • A short MAG1WW60-1 cellular observation did not reproduce the earlier issue. This does not establish a general 5G fix. If engineering requests a modem reproduction, confirm Modem log is enabled and writing continuously before the fault; log collection is not required for ordinary use.
  • USB 480 Mbit/s is the sampled link mode. Use a known data-capable cable and host for further checks; the current result does not identify which component limits the link.
  • If the translation tile is absent, check the firmware and supported enablement path. The test used a temporary engineering-added tile, not a verified default layout.

Evidence sources: functional · system · usb-typec

Find Hub: finding and protecting a lost phone

Find the MAG1 device-finding settings and understand what has been checked before relying on remote recovery.

MAG1WW60-1 · dated captures available

This chapter uses MAG1WW60-1 evidence only. Reference steps are separate from the actions actually recorded.

Settings → Security & privacy → Device finders → Find Hub

Before you start

  • For account-based Find Hub recovery, use the Google Account associated with the phone and keep a way to complete account verification from another device.
  • Check Location and Allow device to be located before the phone is lost. See Google’s preparation reference below.
  • For any demonstration, keep account details, maps, coordinates and other devices out of public captures.

Reference steps · see recorded scope below

  1. Open Settings → Security & privacy → Device finders. The inspected MAG1 showed Find Hub with the summary On.
  2. Open Find Hub and inspect Allow device to be located. It was enabled during the recorded check; no switch was changed.
  3. Open Remote Lock to inspect its separate setting. Use Remote Lock was Off on this device. Return without changing it if you are only reviewing the configuration.
  4. The Find Hub settings page provides Find Hub app and Find Hub web entries. Their presence was confirmed; the demonstration did not open an account device list or map.

Buttons and current settings

OptionObserved state and limits

If your phone is missing — service reference

The following is general Google guidance, not a recorded MAG1 test.

  1. On another device, open Find Hub, sign in to the phone’s Google Account and select the correct phone. Complete any requested identity check.
  2. Review the displayed location and its timestamp. Use Play sound for a nearby phone, or Mark as lost to lock it and provide return details. Availability depends on the service and device state.
  3. Factory reset permanently removes device data and ends further finding through Find Hub; an SD card may not be erased. Treat it as a last resort, not a routine test.

How to read evidence

  • Device metadata identifies what the system reports; it is not a hardware performance or certification test.
  • Static code shows implemented paths and declared configurations; it does not prove successful operation.
  • Historical tests apply to their recorded firmware, app, date and conditions only.
  • Project statements remain attributed specifications. Conflicting developer-build observations are listed for reconciliation, not silently substituted.
  • Pending means no adequate evidence or test yet; it does not automatically mean unsupported or defective.

MAGNE Wallet: versions, networks and safe preparation

Confirmed: package identity, static function paths and current platform services. Not confirmed: creation/import/recovery success, per-chain transfers, signing behavior or compatibility with arbitrary cards and DApps. Static analysis found unresolved security issues. USER and USERDEBUG 1.2.15 share the relevant code; changing the signature alone is not a fix. SE participation does not make the whole Android app a trusted environment. No user-data leak or remote asset theft was demonstrated. Engineering fixes and asset-free re-testing are required before a production-use judgment.

Hardware, ports, buttons and package contents

  • The sample reports a 12 GB RAM class; Linux exposes about 11.14 GiB. Approximately 6.91 GiB of zram is compressed swap, not extra physical RAM.
  • The storage device identifies as WDC SDINFDO4-512G and reports UFS 3.1. Its main block device is about 512.083 GB; /data is about 464.00 GiB before considering used space. These are different units and allocation layers, not a throughput benchmark.
  • The display interface reports 1080 × 2388 and 60/120 Hz modes. The 60 Hz snapshot does not remove the separately observed 120 Hz mode. HDR types are declared capabilities, not measured brightness or certification.
  • This sample has no verified Type-C display output or working ToF ranging. A VL53L0 device object is unbound; the DP transmitter and PTN38003A redriver nodes are disabled. Node presence is not an accessory compatibility result.
  • UMP9620 audio-codec binding supersedes the inference from the legacy sc2730 sound-card name. The wireless-charger names CPS4021/CPS4201 differ and still require BOM confirmation. Exact component models are not substituted for functional tests.

USB file transfer, charging and tethering

  • The unchanged cable/host connection negotiated USB High-Speed: 480 Mbit/s bus signaling, not measured file-copy speed. The controller’s super-speed-plus limit does not prove the external port supports that speed.
  • The connected phone was a data device and power sink. Dual-role/OTG and audio-accessory declarations are present, but USB drives, reverse power and analog adapters were not tested.
  • Local PD revision is 3.0. The driver reported a fixed 5 V / 3 A profile (15 W nominal); this is neither measured absorbed power nor the phone’s maximum charging rating. PPS was not selected or tested.
  • No display was attached. Local DP Alternate Mode registration does not prove a negotiated video link; DP transmitter/redriver nodes are disabled on this build. Do not buy a display adapter on this evidence alone.

Wired charging, wireless charging and battery care

  • On the sampled full battery, the PD node reported 5 V / 3 A while generic power nodes reported 5 V / 2 A. These layers must not be combined into a measured charging result; no external power meter or maximum-power test was used.
  • The fuel-gauge design/full fields both report 4841 mAh. This is a driver estimate/configuration, not a discharge capacity test and not a replacement for the project’s 5000 mAh / up to 33 W wired / 15 W wireless specification. Vendor reconciliation is pending.
  • The raw cycle-count field is not interpretable without the vendor’s unit definition. No battery-health percentage, wireless-charge success or PPS performance has been verified.

Camera, photos, videos and modes

  • MAG1WW60-1, camera 1.0000.19: the recorded test saved one 4080 × 3072 JPEG and a 31.89 s, 1920 × 1080 H.264 video at about 30 fps. Complete file decoding and device/computer hashes passed. Front/rear previews switched successfully; no front photo was saved.
  • A later 16 October capture confirmed More → Ultra res and a 6144 × 8064 image (49.55MP) before adding the Frame watermark. The earlier 12.53MP sample alone did not establish this mode. Front-camera driver naming and public output dimensions likewise describe different layers.
  • A camera-app freezer/Binder exit occurred before the successful capture. It is a recorded issue for investigation, not proof that a sensor or AI algorithm failed. Long recordings, 4K/HDR/EIS combinations, night/portrait/macro and image-quality improvement remain untested here.

Local call translation and the system voice assistant

  • On MAG1WW60-1 with AI app 15.00001.22, a translation tile was temporarily added for a consented automated-service test call. It was absent from the initial Quick Settings layout, so this is not evidence that every user can find it there by default.
  • Enabling translation was followed by increasing NPU task counts; the llm_service process held /dev/vha0 and mapped the Qwen2.5-1.5B model. The user confirmed translation output. This supports NPU use in that tested call-translation path.
  • The second run added 15,121 completed driver tasks including tail work, with no driver failures in its samples. Task counts are not tokens and accumulated execution time is not translation latency.

MAG1WW60-1 local AI

MAG1WW60-1 integrates dedicated camera visual-AI components and a separate local call-translation model path. The camera application and JN1 configuration contain scene-recognition, denoising, depth/segmentation and beauty components. Integration does not establish that every component executes in every mode.

In the MAG1WW60-1 call-translation test, the Qwen2.5-1.5B model service opened the NPU device and completed task counts increased after translation was enabled. This supports NPU use by that translation path. A subsequent DEMO produced new transcripts and translations with Wi-Fi and mobile data disabled; see the recorded test conditions below. The processor used by each ASR/TTS stage was not established.

Camera mode-by-mode runtime tracing remains pending. There is no current evidence that ordinary photography uses the translation language model, or that CPU, GPU and NPU simultaneously execute the same model.

NFC, tapping cards and wallet recovery limits

  • HED NFC and SE services exist, but an external NFC backup card, the embedded SE and the platform TEE have distinct roles. No card model, backup/restore operation, lockout policy or cross-device recovery was validated in this report.
  • The wallet app handles decrypted recovery phrases during display/backup. Do not describe NFC backup as proof that recovery phrases never enter Android. Use only vendor-confirmed cards and wait for the analyzed build’s security fixes and recovery verification.
